surv_bart

bart_survival.surv_bart

High-level API for Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART) survival analysis.

Provides: - SurvBART (alias BartSurvModel): Estimator class with fit, predict, and serialization. - format_survival_data (alias get_surv_pre_train): Preprocess time-to-event data into pooled cross-sections. - format_prediction_data (alias get_posterior_test): Prepare test covariates across prediction time intervals. - compute_survival_curves (alias get_sv_prob): Cumulative product survival probability transformation. - compute_pdp (alias get_pdp): Partial dependence data generation. - compute_causal_pdp (alias get_causal_pdp): Causal G-Computation with support violation audit. - compute_hazard_ratio (alias pdp_rr_metric): Posterior Risk Ratio / Hazard Ratio extraction. - compute_pdp_difference (alias pdp_diff_metric): Posterior marginal survival difference extraction.

class bart_survival.surv_bart.BartSurvModel(trees: int = 50, draws: int = 2500, tune: int = 1000, chains: int = 4, cores: int | None = None, thin: int = 10, thin_idata: bool = False, use_sparsity: bool = False, split_method: str = 'empirical', max_cutpoints: int = 512, update_fraction: float = 1.0, min_node_size: int = 5, k: float = 2.0, alpha: float = 0.95, beta: float = 2.0, sparsity_warmup: int | None = None, unique_midpoints: bool | None = None, split_rules: List[Any] | None = None, split_prior: Any | None = None, model_config: Dict[str, Any] | None = None, sampler_config: Dict[str, Any] | None = None)

Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART) Survival Model (SurvBART).

Implements discrete-time probit hazard modeling using an ensemble of sum-of-trees. Supports warm-started Dirichlet sparsity selection (DART), empirical unique midpoint cutpoints (512 resolution), MCMC thinning, and support-audited Causal G-Computation.

estimate_effect(X: ndarray | DataFrame, primary_col: str | int = 'inpatient', values: List[int | float] | None = None, delta: float | None = None, shift: bool | None = None, times: ndarray | List[float] | None = None, audit_support: bool = True, donor_seed: int | None = 42, event_weights: ndarray | None = None, clip_to_range: bool = False, **kwargs: Any) → Dict[str, Any]

Estimates counterfactual treatment effects using Causal G-Computation and Modified Treatment Policies.

Supports both: 1. Binary / Categorical exposures: Audits conditional support for positivity violations (e.g. deterministic

zeros like LOS=0 for outpatients) and re-routes dependent features to conditional donor resampling.

  1. Continuous exposures: Evaluates a counterfactual shift intervention (Modified Treatment Policy) comparing natural course (X) vs shifted exposure (X + delta). Alternatively evaluates fixed 2-point contrasts if explicit values=[v0, v1] are supplied.

Metrics computed: - Event-weighted summary Hazard Ratio (default, Cox-aligned via complementary log-log link). - Unweighted summary Hazard Ratio across follow-up intervals. - Time-varying Hazard Ratio curve HR(t) via complementary log-log link. - Time-varying discrete risk ratio curve RR_discrete(t) = h1(t) / h0(t) (not averaged). - Time-varying Risk Difference curve RD(t) = Risk_1(t) - Risk_0(t) = S_0(t) - S_1(t) (1 over 0). - Survival Difference curve S_1(t) - S_0(t) = -RD(t). - Event-weighted and unweighted summary Risk Differences. - Final horizon Risk Difference RD(t_end). - Restricted Mean Survival Time (RMST) difference.

Parameters:

  • X (Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]) – Baseline cohort covariates.

  • primary_col (Union[str, int], optional) – Primary exposure variable name or column index. Defaults to “inpatient”.

  • values (Optional[List[Union[int, float]]], optional) – Counterfactual intervention values. If None, auto-detects binary exposures ([0, 1]) or triggers continuous shift intervention.

  • delta (Optional[float], optional) – Shift increment for continuous exposures (X + delta). Defaults to 1.0.

  • shift (Optional[bool], optional) – Force continuous shift intervention mode. Defaults to None.

  • times (Optional[Union[np.ndarray, List[float]]], optional) – Evaluation time points. Defaults to None.

  • audit_support (bool, optional) – Whether to audit and flag support violations. Defaults to True.

  • donor_seed (Optional[int], optional) – Random seed for reproducible donor resampling. Defaults to 42.

  • event_weights (Optional[np.ndarray], optional) – Normalized interval weights for summary HR/RD. Defaults to model’s empirical event_weights_ if available.

  • clip_to_range (bool, optional) – Whether to clip continuous shifted values to observed maximum. Defaults to False.

  • **kwargs – Additional prediction keyword arguments.

Returns:

Dictionary containing weighted and unweighted HRs, RDs, RMST, curves, credible intervals, and draws.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

bart_survival.surv_bart.compute_causal_pdp(x: DataFrame, primary_col: str | int = 'inpatient', values: list = [0, 1], audit_support: bool = True, donor_seed: int | None = 42) → Tuple[ndarray, Dict, List[str]]

Generates counterfactual data for Causal G-Computation with support violation audit.

Identifies dependent features or post-exposure mediators that have structural support or positivity violations with the primary exposure (e.g., deterministic zeros like LOS=0 when Inpatient=0). Performs conditional donor resampling for dependent features while leaving baseline confounders intact, strictly avoiding off-support extrapolation.

Parameters:

  • x (pd.DataFrame) – Baseline covariate dataframe.

  • primary_col (Union[str, int]) – Primary exposure column name or index.

  • values (list, optional) – Counterfactual intervention values. Defaults to [0, 1].

  • audit_support (bool, optional) – Whether to audit and flag support violations. Defaults to True.

  • donor_seed (int, optional) – Random seed for reproducible donor resampling. Defaults to 42.

Returns:

  • out_sk: Stacked counterfactual covariate matrix.

  • c_idx: Index coordinate dictionary compatible with get_posterior_test.

  • dependent_features: List of audited features exhibiting support violations.

Return type:

Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict, List[str]]

bart_survival.surv_bart.compute_hazard_and_risk_difference(pdp_val: Dict[str, ndarray], idx: int, event_weights: ndarray | None = None, qntile: List[float] = [0.025, 0.975], eps: float = 1e-07) → Dict[str, Any]

Computes event-weighted and unweighted Hazard Ratios and Risk Differences from counterfactual predictions.

Contrasts Intervention Arm 1 (obs >= idx) over Reference Arm 0 (obs < idx).

Calculates: - Event-weighted summary Hazard Ratio (default, Cox-aligned via complementary log-log link). - Unweighted summary Hazard Ratio across follow-up intervals. - Time-varying Hazard Ratio curve HR(t) via complementary log-log link. - Time-varying discrete risk ratio curve RR_discrete(t) = h1(t) / h0(t) (not averaged). - Time-varying Risk Difference curve RD(t) = Risk_1(t) - Risk_0(t) = S_0(t) - S_1(t) (1 over 0). - Survival Difference curve S_1(t) - S_0(t) = -RD(t). - Event-weighted and unweighted summary Risk Differences. - Final horizon Risk Difference RD(t_end). - Restricted Mean Survival Time (RMST) difference.

Parameters:

  • pdp_val (Dict[str, np.ndarray]) – Dictionary containing ‘prob’ (hazards) and ‘sv’ (survival curves). Arrays have shape (n_draws, 2 * N, n_times).

  • idx (int) – Split index demarcating Reference Arm 0 (:idx) and Intervention Arm 1 (idx:).

  • event_weights (Optional[np.ndarray], optional) – Normalized event weights per interval. If None, defaults to uniform interval weighting.

  • qntile (List[float], optional) – Credible interval quantiles. Defaults to [0.025, 0.975].

  • eps (float, optional) – Epsilon threshold for numerical safety. Defaults to 1e-7.

Returns:

Comprehensive dictionary containing summary statistics, credible intervals, and draw arrays.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

bart_survival.surv_bart.compute_hazard_ratio(pdp_val: Dict[str, ndarray], idx: int, qntile: List[float] = [0.025, 0.975]) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Returns:

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.compute_shift_pdp(x: DataFrame | ndarray, primary_col: str | int, delta: float = 1.0, clip_to_range: bool = False) → Tuple[ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]

Generates counterfactual datasets for a continuous shift intervention (Modified Treatment Policy).

Contrasts the natural course cohort (Arm 0: X) against a cohort where every individual’s continuous exposure is shifted by delta units (Arm 1: X + delta).

Parameters:

  • x (Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]) – Baseline covariate matrix or DataFrame.

  • primary_col (Union[str, int]) – Continuous variable name or column index to shift.

  • delta (float, optional) – Increment added to primary_col. Defaults to 1.0.

  • clip_to_range (bool, optional) – Whether to clip shifted values to observed maximum. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • out_sk: Stacked counterfactual matrix of shape (2 * N, n_features).

  • c_idx: Index coordinate dictionary demarcating Arm 0 and Arm 1.

Return type:

Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]

bart_survival.surv_bart.compute_survival_curves(post: ndarray | DataArray | Dataset, coords: ndarray) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates discrete-time hazard and cumulative survival probability estimates.

Computes S(t) = prod_{s=1}^t (1 - h(s)) across all posterior draws and subjects.

Parameters:

  • post (Union[np.ndarray, xr.DataArray, xr.Dataset]) – Posterior predictive hazard draws.

  • coords (np.ndarray) – Subject coordinate indices to reshape predictions per subject and time.

Returns:

  • ‘prob’: Hazard probability array of shape (n_draws, n_subjects, n_time_points).

  • ’sv’: Cumulative survival probability array of shape (n_draws, n_subjects, n_time_points).

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.format_survival_data(y_time: ndarray, y_status: ndarray, x: ndarray, weight: ndarray | None = None, time_scale: float | None = None) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates pooled cross-sectional long-format dataset for discrete-time survival training.

Transforms right-censored time-to-event outcomes into person-time binary event observations. Each individual contributes records for discrete intervals $t = 1, 2, dots, T_i$.

Parameters:

  • y_time (np.ndarray) – Array of observed follow-up times.

  • y_status (np.ndarray) – Binary event indicator (1 if event occurred, 0 if right-censored).

  • x (np.ndarray) – Baseline covariate matrix of shape (n_individuals, n_features).

  • weight (Optional[np.ndarray], optional) – Observation weights (e.g. for case-cohort designs). Defaults to 1.0.

  • time_scale (Optional[float], optional) – Time discretization scale (e.g. 5 for 5-day intervals). Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • ‘y’: Binary event indicator array of shape (n_person_time, 1).

  • ’x’: Long-format covariate matrix where column 0 is discrete time, followed by covariates.

  • ’w’: Observation weights aligned with person-time rows.

  • ’coord’: Individual identifier integer array linking person-time rows to subjects.

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_causal_pdp(x: DataFrame, primary_col: str | int = 'inpatient', values: list = [0, 1], audit_support: bool = True, donor_seed: int | None = 42) → Tuple[ndarray, Dict, List[str]]

Generates counterfactual data for Causal G-Computation with support violation audit.

Identifies dependent features or post-exposure mediators that have structural support or positivity violations with the primary exposure (e.g., deterministic zeros like LOS=0 when Inpatient=0). Performs conditional donor resampling for dependent features while leaving baseline confounders intact, strictly avoiding off-support extrapolation.

Parameters:

  • x (pd.DataFrame) – Baseline covariate dataframe.

  • primary_col (Union[str, int]) – Primary exposure column name or index.

  • values (list, optional) – Counterfactual intervention values. Defaults to [0, 1].

  • audit_support (bool, optional) – Whether to audit and flag support violations. Defaults to True.

  • donor_seed (int, optional) – Random seed for reproducible donor resampling. Defaults to 42.

Returns:

  • out_sk: Stacked counterfactual covariate matrix.

  • c_idx: Index coordinate dictionary compatible with get_posterior_test.

  • dependent_features: List of audited features exhibiting support violations.

Return type:

Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict, List[str]]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_pdp(x: ndarray | DataFrame, var_col: List[int | str] = [], values: List[int | float] = [], qt: List[float] = [0.25, 0.5, 0.75], sample_n=None, method: str = 'marginal', audit_support: bool = False) → Tuple[ndarray, Dict] | Tuple[ndarray, Dict, List[str]]

Generates data for Partial Dependency Plots or Causal G-Computation.

Parameters:

  • x (Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]) – Covariate matrix or DataFrame.

  • var_col (List[Union[int, str]], optional) – Covariate column to generate pdp values. Defaults to [].

  • values (List[Union[int, float]], optional) – Values to test on for each covariate. Defaults to [].

  • qt (List[float], optional) – Quantiles to generate values on if none are given. Defaults to [0.25, 0.5, 0.75].

  • sample_n (int, optional) – Sample size of large dataset. Useful for working with large datasets. Defaults to None.

  • method (str, optional) – ‘marginal’ for standard PDP, or ‘causal’ for support-audited G-Computation. Defaults to ‘marginal’.

  • audit_support (bool, optional) – If True, audits for positivity/support violations. Defaults to False.

Returns:

PDP covariate matrix and tracking dictionary.

Return type:

Union[Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict], Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict, List[str]]]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_posterior_test(y_time: ndarray, y_status: ndarray, x: ndarray, time_scale: float | None = None) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates evaluation grid in long-time format for out-of-sample posterior predictions.

Constructs counterfactual cross-product of discrete evaluation times and subject covariates.

Parameters:

  • y_time (np.ndarray) – Follow-up times defining the discrete time evaluation grid.

  • y_status (np.ndarray) – Event indicators (used for historical reference).

  • x (np.ndarray) – Baseline covariate matrix to evaluate.

  • time_scale (Optional[float], optional) – Time discretization scale. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • ‘post_x’: Evaluated covariate matrix with time in column 0.

  • ’coords’: Subject coordinate identifier array.

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_shift_pdp(x: DataFrame | ndarray, primary_col: str | int, delta: float = 1.0, clip_to_range: bool = False) → Tuple[ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]

Generates counterfactual datasets for a continuous shift intervention (Modified Treatment Policy).

Contrasts the natural course cohort (Arm 0: X) against a cohort where every individual’s continuous exposure is shifted by delta units (Arm 1: X + delta).

Parameters:

  • x (Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]) – Baseline covariate matrix or DataFrame.

  • primary_col (Union[str, int]) – Continuous variable name or column index to shift.

  • delta (float, optional) – Increment added to primary_col. Defaults to 1.0.

  • clip_to_range (bool, optional) – Whether to clip shifted values to observed maximum. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • out_sk: Stacked counterfactual matrix of shape (2 * N, n_features).

  • c_idx: Index coordinate dictionary demarcating Arm 0 and Arm 1.

Return type:

Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_surv_pre_train(y_time: ndarray, y_status: ndarray, x: ndarray, weight: ndarray | None = None, time_scale: float | None = None) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates pooled cross-sectional long-format dataset for discrete-time survival training.

Transforms right-censored time-to-event outcomes into person-time binary event observations. Each individual contributes records for discrete intervals $t = 1, 2, dots, T_i$.

Parameters:

  • y_time (np.ndarray) – Array of observed follow-up times.

  • y_status (np.ndarray) – Binary event indicator (1 if event occurred, 0 if right-censored).

  • x (np.ndarray) – Baseline covariate matrix of shape (n_individuals, n_features).

  • weight (Optional[np.ndarray], optional) – Observation weights (e.g. for case-cohort designs). Defaults to 1.0.

  • time_scale (Optional[float], optional) – Time discretization scale (e.g. 5 for 5-day intervals). Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • ‘y’: Binary event indicator array of shape (n_person_time, 1).

  • ’x’: Long-format covariate matrix where column 0 is discrete time, followed by covariates.

  • ’w’: Observation weights aligned with person-time rows.

  • ’coord’: Individual identifier integer array linking person-time rows to subjects.

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_sv_mean_quant(sv: ndarray, msk: ndarray, draws: bool = True, qntile: List[float] = [0.025, 0.975]) → Dict[str, ndarray]

  • draws (bool, optional) – If True, aggregates across posterior draws. Defaults to True.

  • qntile (List[float], optional) – Credible interval quantiles. Defaults to [0.025, 0.975].

Mean and quantile curves for masked and unmasked groups.

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.get_sv_prob(post: ndarray | DataArray | Dataset, coords: ndarray) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates discrete-time hazard and cumulative survival probability estimates.

Computes S(t) = prod_{s=1}^t (1 - h(s)) across all posterior draws and subjects.

Parameters:

  • post (Union[np.ndarray, xr.DataArray, xr.Dataset]) – Posterior predictive hazard draws.

  • coords (np.ndarray) – Subject coordinate indices to reshape predictions per subject and time.

Returns:

  • ‘prob’: Hazard probability array of shape (n_draws, n_subjects, n_time_points).

  • ’sv’: Cumulative survival probability array of shape (n_draws, n_subjects, n_time_points).

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.pdp_diff_metric(pdp_val: Dict[str, ndarray], idx: int, qntile: List[float] = [0.025, 0.975]) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates posterior estimate of marginal survival difference between counterfactual groups.

Parameters:

  • pdp_val (Dict[str, np.ndarray]) – Posterior output dictionary containing ‘sv’.

  • idx (int) – Split index demarcating counterfactual groups in stacked PDP matrix.

  • qntile (List[float], optional) – Quantiles for credible interval. Defaults to [0.025, 0.975].

Returns:

  • ‘diff_m’: Posterior mean survival difference curve across time points.

  • ’diff_q’: Posterior credible interval quantiles of the difference curve.

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]

bart_survival.surv_bart.pdp_hr_rd_metric(pdp_val: Dict[str, ndarray], idx: int, event_weights: ndarray | None = None, qntile: List[float] = [0.025, 0.975], eps: float = 1e-07) → Dict[str, Any]

Computes event-weighted and unweighted Hazard Ratios and Risk Differences from counterfactual predictions.

Contrasts Intervention Arm 1 (obs >= idx) over Reference Arm 0 (obs < idx).

Calculates: - Event-weighted summary Hazard Ratio (default, Cox-aligned via complementary log-log link). - Unweighted summary Hazard Ratio across follow-up intervals. - Time-varying Hazard Ratio curve HR(t) via complementary log-log link. - Time-varying discrete risk ratio curve RR_discrete(t) = h1(t) / h0(t) (not averaged). - Time-varying Risk Difference curve RD(t) = Risk_1(t) - Risk_0(t) = S_0(t) - S_1(t) (1 over 0). - Survival Difference curve S_1(t) - S_0(t) = -RD(t). - Event-weighted and unweighted summary Risk Differences. - Final horizon Risk Difference RD(t_end). - Restricted Mean Survival Time (RMST) difference.

Parameters:

  • pdp_val (Dict[str, np.ndarray]) – Dictionary containing ‘prob’ (hazards) and ‘sv’ (survival curves). Arrays have shape (n_draws, 2 * N, n_times).

  • idx (int) – Split index demarcating Reference Arm 0 (:idx) and Intervention Arm 1 (idx:).

  • event_weights (Optional[np.ndarray], optional) – Normalized event weights per interval. If None, defaults to uniform interval weighting.

  • qntile (List[float], optional) – Credible interval quantiles. Defaults to [0.025, 0.975].

  • eps (float, optional) – Epsilon threshold for numerical safety. Defaults to 1e-7.

Returns:

Comprehensive dictionary containing summary statistics, credible intervals, and draw arrays.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

bart_survival.surv_bart.pdp_rr_metric(pdp_val: Dict[str, ndarray], idx: int, qntile: List[float] = [0.025, 0.975]) → Dict[str, ndarray]

Generates posterior Hazard Ratio / Risk Ratio between counterfactual intervention groups.

Parameters:

  • pdp_val (Dict[str, np.ndarray]) – Posterior output dictionary containing ‘prob’.

  • idx (int) – Split index demarcating counterfactual groups in stacked PDP matrix.

  • qntile (List[float], optional) – Quantiles for credible interval. Defaults to [0.025, 0.975].

Returns:

  • ‘rr_m’: Posterior mean hazard ratio curve across time points.

  • ’rr_q’: Posterior credible interval quantiles of the hazard ratio curve.

Return type:

Dict[str, np.ndarray]
